full_judgment: 7. We shall not concern ourselves with the cases coming under clauses (a), (b) and (e) of the section, clauses (c) and (d) are relevant for our purpose, clause (c) deals with cases which immediately before the commencement of the Ordinance were pending in a Court. Clause (d) deals with cases in which investigation was pending with any police officer immediately before the commencement of the Ordinance. On a careful reading of these two clauses, we are of the opinion that these two clauses are mutually exclusive. When an investigation is pending with a police officer it is covered by subsection (d) and it is not yet a case pending in any court within the meaning of clause (c). A case become pending in any Court only after investigation is over and charge-sheet has been submitted before the court. We are unable to agree with the view of the learned Advocate that on the lodging of the FIR a case becomes a case pending in a court within the meaning of clause (c). It is then a case pending for investigation within the meaning of clause (d). After investigation and. on the submission of charge-sheet before a Court it would become a case pending in Court. However, in the present case, the charge-sheet was submitted to the Court before the date of the Ordinance, and the case was a case pending in Court immediately before the commencement of the Ordinance XXIV of 1982 and is covered by section 35 (c) of the Ordinance and section 339C CrPC. is not attracted, In this view of the matter the learned Additional Sessions Judge has clearly erred in law in taking a view that the case was governed by section 339C CrPC and that the accused persons were entitled to be released. We may add that we are in respectful agreement with the view expressed in the reported decision that the limitation of time as per section 35(c) of the Ordinance XXIV of 1982 is mere directory in nature. For non-disposal of a case within the time specified there no consequence follows and the accused does not become entitled to get released.
